title: Austin OKs New Drive-In Gas Station
summary:
*   The city authorized Magnolia Petroleum Company to build a "modern drive-in auto filling station" at the southwest corner of Lavaca and Fourteenth streets.
*   The station will sell gasoline, lubricating oils, greases, and other automotive products, featuring driveways on both Lavaca and Fourteenth streets for easy vehicle access.
*   This permit is subject to current and future city regulations and can be revoked by the City Council if needed for public safety or other reasons.

SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL: Austin, Texas, Jan. 10, 1919.

The Council met with all members present except Councilman Powell.
The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution: RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL
OF THE CITY OF AUSTIN, TEXAS: That the Magnolia Petroleum Company of Texas be and it is
hereby authorized to erect and maintain on a space of ground about 60 feet by 60 feet at
the southwest corner of Lavaca and Fourteenth streets in this city, a modern drive-in auto
filling station from which it shall be authorized to sell to the trade gasoline,
lubricating oils, greases and other products and accessories. Said Magnolia Petroleum
Company is authorized under this permit to construct a driveway so as to permit ingress
and egress to said station on both Lavaca and Fourteenth streets for automobiles, trucks,
etc., desiring to enter or leave such station, and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED:
That this permit is hereby granted subject to present and future rules, regulations and
ordinances of the City of Austin regulating auto filling stations, and
BE IT RESOLVED FURTHER:
That this permit is granted subject to revocation at any time in the judgment of the City
Council should it become necessary in the police and fire regulations, or for other cause,
to either modify or repeal this permit.
The resolution was adopted by a vote of 4 yeas, no nays, Councilman Powell being absent.
APPROVED, Jan. 10, 1919: A. P. Wooldridge, Mayor.
The Council then adjourned.
